prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 团队周报看板（第 34 周） (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "成员" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 2: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 54px
  col 3: header "本周完成" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 679px
  col 4: header "下周计划" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 934px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"汇总团队成员第 34 周的工作状态、本周完成情况和下周计划，便于识别风险与跟进事项。","reading":"读者先按成员定位一行，再查看状态，并横向对照本周完成与下周计划；也可纵向扫描状态列，快速发现风险和阻塞。两列长文本会形成较高的行，同一行内较短单元格可利用已有高度。","groups":["成员和状态共同构成每行的快速识别区。","本周完成和下周计划都是按成员组织的叙述性工作信息，应便于横向比较；下周计划的最长单行内容更长。"],"keep_intact":["成员姓名和状态标记及文字尽量保持在一行，便于快速识别。","数字、百分比、英文术语和其他不可断开的标识应保持完整。","四列表头尽量各占一行。"],"may_wrap":["本周完成和下周计划中的中文叙述可在自然断点换行。","较短叙述可利用同一行中较长叙述形成的高度。"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[67,75,108,109],"idea":"两列叙述几乎等宽，强调本周与下周的横向对照，同时完整容纳姓名和状态。"},{"name":"B","widths":[67,75,90,127],"idea":"将更多宽度分配给内容更长的下周计划，方便阅读后续行动，本周完成列则承担更多换行。"},{"name":"C","widths":[67,75,128,89],"idea":"优先加宽本周完成列，方便审阅已交付成果，同时保留下周计划列的完整表头。"}]}
